thread:
marcus: proposing API change for per-customer split + isolation guards — need a quick sync. TL;DR: allow a customer-scoped policy with traffic_split + fallback_policy + soft quotas so a noisy tenant can't take down shared pools
anya: sounds reasonable. quick question — should fallback be a model variant (v1/v2) or a routing tier (cheap/fast)? i'd lean model variant for predictable outputs
srinivas: we also need a circuit-breaker at the routing layer. if error_rate > 5% or p99 latency spikes, auto-divert or drop percent to 0.1%. otherwise one bad customer floods the queues
eng-bot: RFC (draft) uploaded: https://go/repo/devex/customer-split-rfc :eyes:
taylor: :thumbsup: i prefer a dedicated policy object vs ad-hoc query params. console needs quick actions: pause, throttle, divert to fallback with audit trail
marcus: console controls should include: pause, ramp-down (time windowed), immediate divert, and a manual 'isolate to reserved pool'. actions are logged and require role checks
dawn: telemetry note — tag every request with customer_id, split_id, variant, rollout_phase. traces should be sampled (1-5%) and we should emit aggregated counters per minute to avoid cardinality explosion
srinivas: proto for policy (PSEUDO JSON):
```
{
  "customer_id": "acme-corp",
  "splits": [
    { "id": "canary-a", "percent": 5, "variant": "v2" },
    { "id": "primary", "percent": 95, "variant": "v1" }
  ],
  "fallback": { "type": "variant", "target": "v1" },
  "guards": { "max_qps": 200, "error_threshold": 0.05 }
}
```
anya: nit: percent as numeric, validate sum <= 100 on write, and add phased ramps (start_ts, end_ts, step_percent) so UX can show schedule
marcus: agree. also need to show "effective routing" in the console (global policy vs customer override ordering). edge case: global low-latency routing may override fallback — needs explicit precedence rules
ops: operational concern — for Dedicated customers we should allow an "isolate" fallback that moves traffic to a reserved GPU pool if errors exceed threshold. we already have reserved pools for enterprise tenants
taylor: UX constraint: "isolate" is effectively destructive (resource shift). put behind modal + ops approval + optional 2FA toggle for extra safety
dawn: alerts/playbook: wire critical routing-ejection alerts to oncall with runbook including `revert-split` and `divert-to-fallback` commands. also add a console quick-playbook snippet
marcus: next steps: i'll update the RFC with API surface + console mocks. srinivas + anya to prototype server-side validator and safety checks. taylor to sketch console actions and approval flows. ops to confirm reserved-pool eject behavior and billing implications
srinivas: sgtm — i'll start a prototype of the validator and a small integration test that simulates noisy tenant blast radius
marcus: thanks everyone — follow up in the RFC thread and i'll drop a short demo next week
srinivas: will ping eng-platform tomorrow morning to hand off the first branch
